lesson: Uniform distance and limits of weights

figures.title: Two all-depth comparisons join into one entire cocycle
figures.caption: The two comparisons e^(-r) phi precedes psi precedes e^r phi at every depth are equivalent to an entire extension U of (D psi : D phi) with norm at most exp(r |Im z|). The upper half-plane is obtained by reflecting and taking adjoints of the extension of the opposite cocycle. The scalar model psi = 2 phi has U(z) = 2^(iz) and distance log 2; its plotted norm attains the envelope on the lower half-plane. This scalar curve illustrates the bound rather than proving the general assertion.
figures.alt: A divided complex plane shows opposite-cocycle reflection across the real axis. A scalar graph compares the norm of 2 to the iz power with the symmetric vertical growth bound.
figures.assumptions: Faithful normal semifinite weights on an arbitrary von Neumann algebra, with r nonnegative. U and the lower-half-plane extension V are the normalized relative cocycles specified in UM3. The scalar graph is a numerical sample of exact formulas. Scalar exact-distance examples assume a nonzero algebra.
figures.kind: analytic mechanism plus exact scalar example

figures.title: One metric bound controls every positive evaluation
figures.caption: For n at least one, h_n = 2^(-n) and k_n^(m) = h_n exp((-1)^n/m) have logarithmic difference of supremum norm exactly 1/m. Thus the associated finite faithful weights converge in the metric, despite their unbounded inverse densities. Every nonzero bounded positive x satisfies e^(-1/m) <= tau_k(x)/tau_h(x) <= e^(1/m). The blue evaluation for x=1 is (2 e^(-1/m) + e^(1/m))/3, using the odd and even h-masses 2/3 and 1/3. The sequence uses integer m; the band is smoothly interpolated from its exact formula.
figures.alt: Alternating logarithmic errors at the first twelve coordinates shrink for m equal to one, two and four. A second plot shows every positive evaluation contained in a multiplicative band converging to one.
figures.assumptions: Counting trace on ell-infinity(N), with N starting at one. The evaluated element x is nonzero, positive and bounded, which gives a finite strictly positive denominator tau_h(x). Panel A displays finite exact samples; the general identity uses the infinite supremum, proved in UM25-UM27. Scalar exact-distance examples assume a nonzero algebra.
figures.kind: exact infinite sequence with labeled finite samples

figures.title: The exact noncommuting distance is log 4
figures.caption: For h = diag(1,3) and k = [[3,1],[1,3]], spectral bounds give both all-power comparisons with scale 4. If 1 <= c < 4, the low spectral subspace of ch at cutoff c is C e1, whereas that of k is either zero or C(1,-1); the required containment therefore fails. The coordinate plot shows the real slices of the two complex lines in the latter case. This exact projection obstruction and the all-power upper bound yield distance log 4.
figures.alt: The spectra of two noncommuting positive matrices, a table of their low spectral ranges, and two distinct lines show why every scale below four fails despite both ranges having rank one in the middle case.
figures.assumptions: The specified positive invertible matrices, usual matrix trace, and c = exp(r) with r nonnegative. The table gives complex spectral ranges. Only the rightmost geometric panel is a real slice, not a depiction of the full four-real-dimensional complex space. Scalar exact-distance examples assume a nonzero algebra.
